title: Sell Mineral Rights in Byesville, OH
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Byesville, OH | Guernsey County
metaDescription: Own mineral rights near Byesville, a former coal town in Guernsey County now sitting on active Utica ground? Get a straightforward, no-obligation cash offer.
heroLead: Byesville built its early economy on coal, and the same land that once hosted deep coal mines now sits over some of Guernsey County's active Utica development.
intro: Byesville's coal history matters for mineral owners in a specific, practical way: a lot of land here has separate coal and oil-and-gas mineral estates, meaning the coal rights and the deeper oil and gas rights may have been severed from the surface, and from each other, at completely different points in history. Before assuming what you own, it's worth confirming which minerals your family's paperwork actually covers.
Setting that history aside, Byesville sits inside Guernsey County's Utica core, and horizontal development has moved steadily through this area for years.

sections.heading: Coal rights versus oil and gas rights
paragraphs: In a lot of eastern Ohio coal country, including around Byesville, a deed might reference 'coal and mining rights' specifically, which is a different, separate estate from oil and gas rights unless the language is broader. If your family's paperwork only discusses coal, your oil and gas rights may have followed a completely different chain of title, possibly staying with the surface owner instead.
A title search at the Guernsey County Recorder's office in Cambridge is the way to sort out exactly which mineral estate, or estates, your family holds today.

sections.heading: Current Utica activity around Byesville
paragraphs: If your oil and gas rights are confirmed and currently leased, your division order and royalty statements are the clearest measure of value, showing your decimal interest and recent production. Guernsey County has had consistent horizontal well activity for years, so most producing tracts here have a real payment history to work from.

sections.heading: Old coal-era severances and dormancy
paragraphs: Because so much of this land has changed hands since its coal mining days, it's not unusual for an oil and gas interest to have sat quiet for decades without anyone in the family realizing it. If that describes your situation, it's worth checking whether Ohio's Dormant Mineral Act could apply, an interest unused for 20 years with no lease, production, or recorded claim to preserve can be reclaimed by the surface owner under ORC 5301.56.

faqs.question: Does my family's old coal lease near Byesville cover oil and gas too?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily. Coal rights and oil and gas rights are often separate mineral estates, so the lease language needs to be reviewed to determine what it actually covers.

faqs.question: How do I find out if my oil and gas rights were ever severed separately?
faqs.answer: A title search at the Guernsey County Recorder's office will trace the full history of severances on your tract, coal, oil and gas, or both.

faqs.question: Is Byesville a strong area for current Utica activity?
faqs.answer: Yes, it sits within Guernsey County's core, which has seen steady horizontal development for years.
